documents.title: Shareholder Meeting / Postal Ballot-Outcome of EGM
Compliances-Certificate under Reg. 74 (5) of SEBI (DP) Regulations, 2018

analysis.summary: SK Minerals & Additives Limited reported a 50% increase in revenue to Rs. 318 crores for FY26, alongside higher EBITDA and PAT. Management highlighted growth driven by strategic material sourcing, volume expansion, and venturing into new segments such as polymer additives. The company plans to invest approximately Rs. 20 crores in capex over the next two years to scale up manufacturing capacity to 18,000 metric tons.

guidance.claim: Management expects the manufacturing contribution to turnover to reach 50% over the next two to three years.
guidance.quote: Currently, 23% of our revenue comes from the manufacturing capabilities, but in the next two to three years, we want to scale the manufacturing contribution to turnover to 50%, with overall increase in turnover also.

guidance.claim: The company aims to increase total manufacturing capacity to 18,000 metric tons in a phased manner over the next 12 to 18 months.
guidance.quote: Basically, we are looking at total capacity of 18,000 metric tons including all the current capacity and this we are going to increase in the phased manner in the next 18 months.

demand_outlook.claim: Management noted that raw material prices and volumes increased significantly starting from December and February.
demand_outlook.quote: So, as we have came out with an IPO and we have working capital available with us, and we have good amount of funds available. So, we have sourced the material for next six months or suddenly there was demand from December onwards of these raw materials and the prices have increased tremendously in February of these raw materials.

demand_outlook.claim: The company is experiencing strong interest and inquiries from both domestic and international buyers for its halogen-free flame retardant products.
demand_outlook.quote: As currently, we are getting a few queries from the international buyers also.

capex_expansion.claim: The 9.6-acre land acquired by the company is intended for developing polymer additives and compounding facilities.
capex_expansion.quote: First of all, this 9.6 acre land which we have taken is for developing our polymer additives and polymer compound facility, whereas specified that in next 12 to 18 months, we will be taking our manufacturing capabilities to 18,000 metric tons.

margins_costs.claim: EBITDA margins increased from 9% to 10% and PAT margins increased from 5% to 6% in FY26.
margins_costs.quote: Our financial performance, which is last financial year we have closed is Rs. 318 crores we have closed and this is 50% growth from the Financial Year ‘25 and our EBITDA margins have increased from 9% to 10% and PAT has increased from 5% to 6%.

margins_costs.claim: Gross margins for manufacturing stand at approximately 30%, while trading products yield about 21%.
margins_costs.quote: One is manufacturing, and second is into trading. So, in terms of gross margin, which we make from manufacturing, right now it's 30%. Whereas, in terms of our trading product, it is 21%.

margins_costs.claim: Polymer additives are expected to yield margins of around 40%.
margins_costs.quote: Currently, in terms of the manufacturing margins, we are standing at 30% approximately, whereas from polymer additives, we feel that the margins would be 40%.

orders_capacity.claim: Total installed capacity stood at 6,600 metric tons.
orders_capacity.quote: The current capacity is 6600 metric tons.

orders_capacity.claim: Out of the total order book, Rs. 42 crores is from government contracts with the rest coming from private customers.
orders_capacity.quote: Out of these Rs. 55 crores, Rs. 42 crores is from government and rest is from private.

orders_capacity.claim: Sales volume reached 46,000 metric tons in FY26, including 4,400 metric tons of manufactured products.
orders_capacity.quote: So, the volume was 33,000 metric ton in FY25 and this year it was 46,000 metric ton in 2026, which comprises of 4,400 metric ton of manufacturing capabilities.

capital_allocation.claim: The company utilizes bank credit lines and IPO proceeds for capital expenditure.
capital_allocation.quote: We have the credit lines available for CAPEX from the banks also. And we have some part of the IPO proceeds which we have raised for CAPEX. So, we will utilize both for taking our capacity to next level to 18,000 metric tons.

capital_allocation.claim: The current working capital cycle is approximately 110 days.
capital_allocation.quote: Currently, working capital cycle is of 110 days.

risks_headwinds.claim: Geopolitical scenarios impact the timeline of raw material arrivals and dry up import trading stock.
risks_headwinds.quote: So, it depends upon the geopolitical scenario. It depends upon the timeline of reaching in India because you never know what is happening throughout the world.

risks_headwinds.claim: The new polymer additives plant is currently experiencing some teething problems.
risks_headwinds.quote: In terms of polymer additives, we have recently set up 400 metric ton plant per month, but there are some teething problems going on which we will try to address in the next three months and that will be also utilized fully in the next six months’ timeline.

management_commitments.claim: Management plans to scale manufacturing capacity to 18,000 metric tons in a phased manner over the next 12 to 18 months.
management_commitments.quote: So, from the current capacity of 600 metric ton, we will take it to 18,000 metric ton in phase manner of next 12 to 18 months.

management_commitments.claim: Management intends to file three patents within the next six months.
management_commitments.quote: But in next six months, we will try to file three patents.

management_commitments.claim: Management targets scaling the manufacturing contribution to turnover to 50% over the next two to three years.
management_commitments.quote: Currently, 23% of our revenue comes from the manufacturing capabilities, but in the next two to three years, we want to scale the manufacturing contribution to turnover to 50%, with overall increase in turnover also.

_meta.note: Facts are verbatim-grounded against the company's own documents; claims whose quote was not found were dropped.
